catalog_quote: Stress Stress in Sambalpuri does not appear to be phonemic. Word when uttered in isolation is generally stressed and the initial syllable of each breath group bears stress. Example /mor bOhigurakO ine Oche/ 'my books are here' /mor pomane iskule jaichOn / 'my sons have gone to school' /ame sOmundOrku jhuri marijisũ/ 'we go to the sea to catch fish' The breath group may contain either one or more than one word.

Example /mor bOhigurakO ine Oche/ 'my books are here' /mor pomane iskule jaichOn/ 'my sons have gone to school' /ame sOmundOrku jhuri marijisũ/ 'we go to the sea to catch fish' The breath group may contain either one or more than one word.' No stress marks are printed on the examples. Preceding sections on the same page (Length: vowel length non-phonemic, rhythm-dependent) and on printed p. 79…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive. The initial syllable of each breath group (a phonological phrase of one or more words) is stressed; a word uttered in isolation forms its own breath group and so carries stress on its first syllable. Within a multi-word breath group, non-initial words are not described as bearing stress of their own.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Hedged wording ('does not appear to be phonemic', 'generally stressed').
new_statements.domain_note: The source's domain is the breath group, not the word: the only word-level claim is that an isolated word 'is generally stressed'. Read as fixed: initial syllable for citation forms; an alternative reading is phrase-level prominence only. Three sentence examples are given; the stress mark is not clearly reproduced in the scan. The vowel-length section on the same page says length is non-phonemic and rhythm-dependent.
new_statements.identity_note: Datta 2002 describes the 'Sambalpuri dialect' of Oriya spoken in Sambalpur, Sundargarh, Bolangir, Kalahandi and the Baudh sub-division of Phulbani (1991 census mother tongue 'Sambalpuri', 40,519 returns) — this is samb1325 / ISO spv proper (Kosli / Western Odia); no sub-dialect is singled out.
